ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Apple vinegar is made by fermentation using apple juice as the raw material. Answer the following question: The respiratory metabolic pathway of yeast is shown in the figure. Processes ① and ② in the figure are the first stage of apple vinegar production. In what place in the yeast cell do they take place?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: On the left side of the figure is “glucose”, which is converted through the arrow labeled ① into the intermediate product “pyruvate”; pyruvate is then converted through the arrow labeled ② into “ethanol + CO₂” on the right side. The figure also shows that pyruvate can be related to “H₂O + CO₂” through another pathway, but this question asks about ① and ②. Then reason: Process ① is the decomposition of glucose into pyruvate, belonging to the glycolysis process; process ② is the conversion of pyruvate into ethanol and carbon dioxide, belonging to yeast alcoholic fermentation. Both of these processes occur in the cytoplasmic matrix of yeast cells. Therefore, in the first stage of apple vinegar production, the place where ① and ② in the figure take place is the cytoplasmic matrix.
